topic: Why Sanad offices — 100% Omani-staffed, government-mandated — are the most important B2B channel in Oman that nobody has built software for yet
format: Client trust story: the Sanad office that started giving every client a portal to track their own cases — what happened to client retention and referrals in the first three months
post:
One Sanad office manager told me something I've been thinking about for weeks.

She was handling 20 client companies. 40 work permits. 15 visa renewals. 8 MOL filings. All of it tracked across WhatsApp groups and a shared Excel file that three people were editing at the same time.

Her words: "Every morning I open my phone and I already feel behind."

Then she gave every client a portal to track their own cases.

Within three months, her clients stopped calling to ask "where is my file?" They started calling to refer her to other businesses instead.

That shift — from reactive to trusted — didn't come from hiring more staff. It came from one structural change: clients could see their own cases moving in real time.

This is exactly what 924 licensed Sanad offices in Oman are missing right now. Not effort. Not capability. Just the right infrastructure.

Work permit tracking Oman businesses expect today isn't a luxury. It's the baseline for client retention.

The Sanad offices that figure this out first will own the market. The rest will stay capped at however many clients one person can manage by memory.

The gap is real. And it's still wide open.
